contract.note: The broad reading is fair: the statement does not limit its conclusion to recursive replacement or unfiltered data. Large synthetic fine-tuning datasets ordinarily satisfy the volume condition.

evidence.note: Microsoft researchers report improved held-out coding performance after substantial synthetic fine-tuning. This supplies a useful-training counterexample, although it is developer-authored research rather than independent validation.
Supports harm under recursive training dominated by generated data. Its assumptions do not establish that substantial synthetic content is generally useless or harmful.
Accumulation avoids collapse in the tested settings. Avoiding degradation alone does not establish useful learning and therefore does not independently refute the useless-or-harmful assertion.

reviews.rationale: The substantial synthetic coding dataset produces useful performance improvements, contradicting the general claim under the fair contract. Recursive-collapse evidence establishes a harmful procedure, but does not rescue the broader assertion.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the cumulative claim about demonstrated capabilities. Its historical endpoint is publication.

contract.note: In the surrounding discussion of business value, materially useful work beyond publicity is a fair ordinary reading. Requiring an entirely unprecedented activity would introduce a stronger novelty criterion the speaker did not specify.

evidence.note: The fixed 2023 research version reports a 14% increase in customer-support productivity and other practical benefits, publicly demonstrated before the statement.

The dated institutional summary reports randomized writing-task speed and quality gains. Limited context requirements and absent factual verification restrict generalization, but do not erase the demonstrated benefits.

reviews.rationale: Before publication, measured customer-support and writing results demonstrated material practical benefits beyond fundraising and publicity. These studies do not establish universal usefulness or unprecedented task categories, neither of which the fair practical reading requires.

contract.note: Meaningful correctness improvements fairly count as progress. The context supports interpreting the scarce stock as human-generated material; the statement supplies no requirement that progress eliminate all unreliability.

evidence.note: DeepMind researchers report improved held-out self-correction using existing problems and self-generated traces. This tests the asserted necessity without an expanded human-data stock; it is developer-authored experimental evidence.

Controlled revision and inference-compute comparisons improve checked mathematical answers using existing data. Specialized training limits broader conclusions but does not require the asserted larger human-data stock.
Documents substantial errors in earlier programming answers. It supports the reliability concern but does not test the claimed necessary condition for improvement.

reviews.rationale: The experiments demonstrate meaningful correctness gains through self-generated training and inference changes using existing human datasets. That contradicts the claimed data necessity under the fair progress criterion. Persistent errors and the absence of universal reliability do not establish that necessity.
